reason: This passage from the Plagues narrative (Exodus 8-10) focuses on God's demonstrations of power against Pharaoh through successive plagues (frogs, flies, boils, hail, locusts, and darkness). While Aaron is mentioned once in a neutral context ('And the Lord said to Moses and to Aaron'), priests are not depicted or characterized in this passage. The passage contrasts God's power with Pharaoh's resistance and briefly shows the Egyptian magicians (חַרְטֻמִּים) failing to stand before Moses due to boils. Priests as a group or institutional role are neither prominently featured nor depicted favorably or unfavorably in this text.
